question.problem:
The following table shows the water flow rate, $R(t),$ through a pipe (in liters per minute) over a period of $40$ minutes.

| $t\,\text{(minutes)}$ | $0$ | $10$ | $20$ | $30$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R\,\text{(liters/minute)}$ | $12$ | $15$ | $17$ | $16$ | $14$ |

Use the right Riemann sum for $R(t)$ over the interval $[0,40]$ with four subintervals to approximate the total volume of water pumped.

The total volume is 
{{field-1}} liters.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the step size $Δt,$ which is just the width of each rectangle. In this case, the endpoints of our interval are $a=0$ and $b=40,$ and there are $n=4$ rectangles, so the step size is

$$
Δt=\frac{b-a}{n}=\frac{40-0}{4}=10.
$$

The area $A$ under the graph can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{R(10)+R(20)+R(30)+R(40)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $R(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $10$ | $20$ | $30$ | $40$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R(t)$ | $15$ | $17$ | $16$ | $14$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(15+17+16+14)\cdot 10 \\  & =62\cdot 10 \\  & =620\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total volume of water pumped over a period of $40$ minutes. So, the total volume is $620$ liters.
